DA  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 3646 of 2009  ==========================================================
 BIPINBHAI MAGANBHAI PATEL  Versus  GORDHANBHAI MAHIJIBHAI TADVI C/O PLATE-WELL PROCESS & &
 ORS.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR MTM HAKIM(1190) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  MR SUNIL B PARIKH(582) for the Defendant(s) No. 3  MR.VARUN K.PATEL(3802) for the Defendant(s) No. 2  RULE SERVED for the Defendant(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 10/10/2024  ORAL ORDER 1. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 01.02.2008 passed in MACP No.495 of 1992 by learned MACT Tribunal (Auxi.), Vadodara, the original claimant has preferred this appeal under section 173 of the Act, whereby, learned Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition.
2. Facts of the case are as under :-
2.1. That on 08.05.1991, the claimant was present at his work place and he was assigned work to bring water from tanker The claimant was sitting on tanker attached with tractor and while coming back, driver of the tractor was driving the tractor in rash and negligent manner and as a result of which, tractor went on divider and wheel of tanker came on left leg of the claimant and he received serious injuries.

Therefore, he filed claim petition NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined claiming compensation.

3. Heard learned advocate Mr.Hakim for the claimants, learned advocate Mr.Varun Patel and learned advocate Mr.Sunil Parekh for respondent nos.2 and 3 respectively.
4.

Learned advocate Mr.Hakim would submit that learned Tribunal has committed gross error in dismissing claim petition on the ground that the claimants have not filed FIR and not produced any evidence on record to indicate that claimant has received injury from the road accident and that road accident has happened.

It is submitted that learned Tribunal has discarded order passed by this Court in Special Civil Application No.3782 of 2000, whereby, this Court while setting aside the order passed by the learned Labour Court permitted the petitioner to approach Workman Compensation Commissioner under the Workman Compensation Act, which by itself indicates road accident has taken place and claimant received injury from road accident.

4.1. Learned advocate Mr.Hakim submits that instead of preferring petition for claiming compensation under Compensation Act, the claimant has chosen forum of MACT in view of section 167 of the Act, 1998.

It is submitted that in this circumstances, since it is established on record that claimant has received injury from road accident, learned Tribunal ought to have granted compensation to the claimant.

4.2. Taking this Court through factual aspect of the case, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined learned advocate Mr.Hakim submits that as per pleadings, on 08.05.1991, the claimant was sitting on the tanker part as he was give duty to fill water in the tanker attached with tractor, at that time, driver of the tractor was driving in rash and negligent manner.
The tractor climbed on divider, the claimant fell down from tanker and at that time, wheel of tanker ran over his legs, so accident happened.

So it clearly establish that due to rash and negligent driving of opponent no.1, claimant received injury but the learned Tribunal believed that since no FIR is filed and no evidence is lead, claimant failed to prove road accident and injury received therefrom.
4.3. Taking this Court through written statement filed by the owner of the vehicle, it is submitted that in clear terms owner of the vehicle has admitted fact of road accident.
Therefore, learned Tribunal was required to pass award against owner of the vehicle but has committed serious error in dismissing the claim petition.
4.4. On above submissions, learned advocate Mr.Hakim submits to allow this appeal and remand the matter for fresh hearing.
5. Against above submissions, learned advocate Mr.Patel for respondent no.2 would submit that claim petition filed before the learned Tribunal is frivolous.
It is Bipinbhai Maganbhai Patel vs Gordhanbhai Mahijibhai Tadvi C/O ...

2 submitted that in the written statement, nowhere clear admission has been stated by the owner.

It is submitted that claimant has already received compensation under ESI and that fact has been stated in the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined written statement by the owner but it could be treated as unclear and unambiguous admission on the part of the owner to accept its liability under Motor Vehicles Act and therefore, learned Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition.

6. Learned advocate Mr.Parekh for Insurance Company after adopting arguments of learned advocate Mr.Patel would submit that in SCA No.3782 of 2000 which was preferred by the owner of the vehicle against judgment and award of learned Labour Court granting compensation under Workman Compensation Act, permitted the claimant to file necessary application under the Workman Compensation Act .

This Court passed this order having invited by learned advocate for the claimant, so in view of that aspect, the claimant was required to file necessary proceedings before the Workman Compensation Act and not before the MACT Tribunal, more particularly,
in absence of documentary evidence on record that due to involvement of use of vehicle claimant has sustained injuries.
6.1. Making above submissions, it is submitted to dismiss the first appeal.
7. Having heard learned advocates for both the sides, at the outset, let refer written statement filed by opponent no.2 in the claim petition at Exh.20.

Para 10 of the written statement reads as under :-
"10.
It is true that the applicant was admitted at GORVA ESI Hospital and was treated with ESI Hospital.
It is not NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined true that the applicant has permanent disablement and received treatment for pain, shock and agony.
It is further not correct to say that applicant had to spend huge amount towards special diet, transportation and other expenses.
It is not correct to say that the applicant had to spend for caretaker at Rs.150/- per day and has to spend huge amount towards special diet, transportation and other expenses.
It is submitted by the opponent that the applicant has already been paid Rs.9545/- way of sickness benefit from ESI department for the reasons mentioned above.
The applicant is not entitled to claim Rs.1,50,000/- by way of compensation, cost and interest and also on the ground of pain, shock and agony.

"
8. Perusing para 10 of the Written Statement, it does not prove unclear and unambiguous admission on the part of the owner to earmark his responsibility under the Motor Vehicles Act and therefore,
judgment cannot be delivered based on conditional admission in the written statement (see : Rajesh Mitra @ Rajesh Kumar Mitra v/s. Karnnani Properties Ltd. - 2024 LiveLaw 790).

sentences.text: Therefore, the contention raised by learned advocate Mr.Hakim that since owner of the vehicle has admitted factum of road accident and learned Tribunal was alteast required to pass award against owner cannot be accepted.
Since the claim petition is filed under section 166 of M.V.Act, the claimant is Bipinbhai Maganbhai Patel vs Gordhanbhai Mahijibhai Tadvi C/O ...

3 required to prove rash and negligent driving by driver of offending vehicle resulting into injury,
which further resulted into permanent disability or partial disability.

In the case on hand, the claimant has not produced single document to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined indicate that road accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by driver of offending vehicle.
Medical papers produced on record at Exh.38 to 41 also fails to demonstrate that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the claimant has received injury.

Though in his deposition, Dr.Mahesh Patel at Exh.43 stated that claimant has received injury from road accident, he fairly admitted that he has issued disability certificate after 8 years of road accident and he has no medical papers.

According to this Court,
claimant failed to prove his case.
9. Moreover, order passed by this Court in Special Civil Application No.3782 of 2000 is required to be referred.

The said petition was preferred by opponent no.2 employer against judgment and award passed by Labour Court in Reference (LC) No.498 of 1997 claiming that Rs.60,000/- granted in favour of workman, despite the workman having admitted domestic / departmental inquiry was unjustified.

Order dated 16.07.2007 passed in Special Civil Application No.3782 of 2000 demonstrate that learned advocate Mr.Hakim argued before the Co-ordinate Bench that workman has suffered injury during course of his employment and as such, workman had already made application before the Commissioner under the Workman Compensation Act (para 6 of the judgment).

Considering this submission, Co-ordinate Bench in its order in para 9 and 10 has observed as under :-
"9.

In the present case, the learned court below neither held that the inquiry was invalid nor did it record a finding NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined that the punishment was shockingly disproportionate.

If that was so, the Labour Court could not assume any jurisdiction to award monetary benefits or monetary compensation in favour of the workman,
simply on the ground that the workman had suffered some injuries during the course of his employment.
10.So far as the award of the compensation against the sufferance of the injuries is concerned, the workman had already gone before the Commissioner, Workmen Compensation.
The said Commissioner would have absolute discretion to make the award.
In the present case, the Labour Court could not make any award in favour of the workman."

10. It is significant to note that learned advocate Mr.Hakim at the relevant time made clear statement that claimant has approached Commissioner for Workman Compensation for getting compensation as claimant had suffered injury during course of his employment.

On going through the pleadings of the claim petition, it is to observe that no such pleadings are made by the claimant clarifying that what happened to application filed before the Commissioner for Workman Compensation nor has stated anything on oath or in his oral evidence.
Learned advocate Mr.Hakim arguing the matter even did not point out during arguments as to what happened to the application made to the Commissioner for Workman Compensation.

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, what appears that claimant NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3646/2009 ORDER DATED: 10/10/2024 undefined petition suffers from vice of suppressing material facts.

It also appears that though claimant categorically stated before the Co- ordinate Bench that he also already filed petition under Workman Compensation Act but he has also preferred Motor Accident Claim Petition and then appeal also.
12. Learned Tribunal has discussed the issue and rightly rejected the claim petition.
I see no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and award.
This Court thinks fit to observe that greedy claimant by suppressing material facts approached learned Tribunal by adopting unscuttle tactics.
The claim petition is found to be frivolous and vexatious and as such the appeal needs to be dismissed with cost.

13. For the foregoing reasons, the First Appeal is dismissed with cost of Rs.3000/-, to be paid to District Legal Services Authority, Vadodara within one week from today by the appellant / claimant,
failing which, amount of cost shall be recovered from claimant by way of arrears of land revenue and DLSA, Vadodara to issue necessary certificate to the Collector directing him to recover amount of cost from the appellant and deposit the same before it.
